****[[Islamabad Memorandum]]

***[[2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries]]
****[[2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain]]
*****The [[Royal Bahraini Army|Bahraini Army]] says on [[X (social network)|X]] that [[Bahrain]] has successfully intercepted and destroyed "a number" of [[Iran]]ian [[Ballistic missile program of Iran|missiles]] and drone attacks on the country. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/bahrain-says-it-intercepted-a-number-of-iranian-aerial-attacks/3980208 (AA)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/bahrain-says-it-was-targeted-by-missiles-drones-in-treacherous-iranian-attacks/ (AFP via ''The Times of Israel'')]
****[[Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war|2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait]]
*****[[Kuwait]]'s [[Chief of the General Staff (Kuwait)|Chief of the General Staff]] says that [[Kuwait Armed Forces|his forces]] have activated [[air defense]] systems to intercept missiles and drones. [https://timeskuwait.com/kuwaiti-air-defenses-intercept-hostile-missile-and-drone-attacks/ (''Times Kuwait'')]
****[[Iran]]'s [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] says it has carried out retaliatory strikes against [[United States]] [[United States Armed Forces|military]] bases in Bahrain and [[List of United States Army installations in Kuwait|Kuwait]], including the [[Ali Al Salem Air Base]] and [[United States Fifth Fleet|U.S. Fifth Fleet]] [[naval base]]. [https://thenewregion.com/posts/5746 (''The New Region'')]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[South Korea]]'s [[Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries|ocean ministry]] says that two more vessels have transited through the [[Strait of Hormuz]], bringing the total amount of ships to do so to 23 after weeks of disruption caused by the war. The ocean ministry also says that only three more South Korean-operated ships are remaining in the [[Persian Gulf]], including the [[Panama]]–[[Flag of convenience|flagged]] ''[[HMM (company)|HMM]] Namu'', which was damaged in an explosion on May 4. [https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10790440 (''The Korea Herald'')]

****[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Iran)|Iranian foreign minister]] [[Abbas Araghchi]] arrives in [[Baghdad]], [[Iraq]], for talks with [[Federal government of Iraq|Iraqi authorities]] on arrangements for the [[State funeral of Ali Khamenei|funeral]] of [[Assassination of Ali Khamenei|former]] [[Supreme Leader of Iran|supreme leader]] [[Ali Khamenei]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iranian-foreign-minister-heads-to-baghdad-for-talks-with-iraqi-officials/3980192 (AA)] [https://www.kurdistan24.net/en/story/922501/abbas-araghchi-arrives-in-iraq-for-khamenei-funeral-coordination (Kurdistan24)]

***[[Gaza peace plan#By Israel|Gaza war ceasefire violations]]
****[[Israel]] reports that it has killed three [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] [[Palestinian Civil Police Force|police]] officers in a latest violation of the [[ceasefire]]. [https://menafn.com/1111323160/Israeli-Forces-Kill-Three-Palestinian-Police-Officers-in-Gaza-Amid-Ceasefire-Tensions (MENAFN)]
***Israel says [[Israel Defense Forces|its military]] has killed Mansour Sami Mahmoud Shahtout, a [[Hamas]] naval police commander who ran the Central Camps and took part in the [[October 7 attacks]], in an [[airstrike]] in the [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/top-commander-in-hamas-naval-police-oct-7-terrorist-killed-in-recent-strikes-idf/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**[[2026 Lebanon war]]
***[[Israeli occupation of Southern Lebanon (2026)|Israeli occupation of Southern Lebanon]]
****Israel says its military has destroyed a [[Hezbollah tunnels|Hezbollah tunnel]] in [[Majdal Zoun]], [[southern Lebanon]], after notifying the United States. Israeli officials state that the {{convert|200|m|ft|adj=on}} tunnel contained [[List of military equipment of Hezbollah|weapons]] and [[rocket launcher]] shafts. [https://www.daily-sun.com/world/883018/israel-says-destroyed-200m-long-hezbollah-tunnel-in-s-lebanon (AFP via ''Daily Sun'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-destroys-hezbollah-underground-infrastructure-southern-lebanon-2026-06-28/ (Reuters)]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[2026 Mali offensives]]
***The [[Human Rights Watch]] reports abuses committed against civilians in [[Mali]] by the [[Al-Qaeda]]-backed [[Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin]], [[Tuareg people|Tuareg]] fighters of the [[Azawad Liberation Front]], the [[Malian Armed Forces#Army|Malian Army]], and [[Russia]]'s [[Africa Corps (Russia)|Africa Corps]] since fighting escalated in April 2026. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa/20260701-human-rights-watch-reports-grave-abuses-from-all-sides-in-mali-since-april-attacks (AFP via RFI)] [https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/06/28/mali-grave-abuses-amid-renewed-fighting (HRW)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian forces]] launch [[FP-5 Flamingo]] [[cruise missile]]s at strategic targets in [[Russia]], striking the [[Titan-Barrikady]] complex in [[Volgograd]], which produces launchers for Russia's [[RS-24 Yars|Yars]] and [[9K720 Iskander|Iskander missile systems]]. Authorities say ten people have been wounded in the strikes. A [[Crimea attacks (2022–present)|separate missile strike]] destroys a [[Pantsir missile system]] in occupied [[Crimea]]. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2026/06/27/ukrainian-flamingos-strike-major-russian-missile-plant/ (''The Telegraph'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''

The passengers are identified as five instructors and five students. '''International relations'''
*[[Armenia–Israel relations]], [[Armenian genocide recognition]]
**[[Thirty-seventh government of Israel|Israel's government]] unanimously approves recognition of the [[World War I]]-era [[Armenian genocide|mass killings]] of [[Armenians]] by the [[Ottoman empire]] as [[genocide]], pending [[Knesset|parliamentary]] ratification. [https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2026/06/28/israel-government-recognizes-armenian-genocide-in-rebuke-to-turkey_6754948_4.html (AFP via ''Le Monde'')] [https://apnews.com/article/israel-turkey-armenian-genocide-ottoman-deaths-5adadfde8f5d68878190594e7f87a1ab (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Crime in Israel]]
**Five people are killed and a child is injured in [[car bomb]]ing attacks and [[Homicide in Israeli law|murder]]s in [[Tel Aviv]], [[Holon]], and [[Arab citizens of Israel|Arab-Israeli]] communities in [[Israel]]. The attacks are linked to [[organized crime]] or criminal violence. [https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/five-killed-suspected-crime-spree-152728880.html (DPA via Yahoo News)]
*[[Iraqi Armed Forces|Iraqi forces]] raid the [[Green Zone]] in [[Baghdad]], [[Iraq]], reportedly arresting at least 47 officials suspected of [[Corruption in Iraq|corruption]], including [[Council of Representatives (Iraq)|lawmakers]] and senior [[Federal government of Iraq|government]] officials. Videos on [[social media]] appear to show [[Iraqi Ground Forces|Iraqi Army]] tanks entering the diplomatic district. The military also begins arresting officials in [[Saladin Governorate|Salahuddin]], [[Al Anbar Governorate|Al Anbar]], and [[Nineveh Governorate|Nineveh]]. [https://www.i24news.tv/en/news/middle-east/artc-iraqi-forces-raid-baghdad-s-green-zone-in-anti-corruption-sweep-targeting-senior-politicians-report (i24 News)] [https://www.kurdistan24.net/en/story/922615/iraqi-state-media-47-lawmakers-and-officials-arrested-in-corruption-probe (Kurdistan24)] [https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/report-iraqi-army-enters-baghdads-green-zone-tanks-deployed (''Middle East Eye'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Bangkok gubernatorial election]]
**[[Chadchart Sittipunt]] is reelected to a second term as [[Governor of Bangkok|governor]] of [[Bangkok]], [[Thailand]]. [https://thediplomat.com/2026/06/bangkoks-voters-hand-chadchart-second-term-as-governor-by-decisive-margin/ (''The Diplomat'')] [https://world.thaipbs.or.th/detail/chadchart-sweeps-to-second-term-as-bangkok-governor/61841 (Thai PBS)]
*[[2026 New Caledonian legislative election]]
**[[New Caledonia]]ns vote to elect 54 seats of [[Congress of New Caledonia|Congress]] for the first time since [[2019 New Caledonian legislative election|2019]], after the vote was delayed three times following [[2024 New Caledonia unrest|unrest]] in 2024 and the [[Bougival Accord]] in 2025. Preliminary results indicate the loyalist bloc taking 24 seats and the separatist bloc taking 26 seats, with [[Oceanian Awakening]] taking a [[crossbench]] position with four seats. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/pacific/632442/heavy-security-deployed-as-new-caledonia-s-crucial-elections-begin (RNZ)] [https://la1ere.franceinfo.fr/nouvellecaledonie/direct-elections-provinciales-2026-en-nouvelle-caledonie-resultats-taux-de-participation-reactions-suivez-la-soiree-electorale-sur-nc-la-1ere-1714798.html (''France Info'')]
*[[Mass media in Uganda]]
**[[Uganda]]'s [[Uganda People's Defence Force|military]] surrounds the offices of [[Nation Media Group]] outlets in [[Kampala]] after army chief [[Muhoozi Kainerugaba]] orders the shutdown of the company's newspapers, television station, and radio networks. [https://www.thedailystar.net/news/world/news/uganda-army-chief-shuts-down-leading-independent-media-group-4210221 (AFP via ''The Daily Star'')]
*The [[Government of the United Kingdom|British government]] announces that it will scrap the 202-year-old [[Vagrancy Act 1824|Vagrancy Act]] that criminalizes [[Homelessness in the United Kingdom|rough sleeping]] in [[England and Wales]], saying that a new law will aim at "preventing homelessness" rather than "punishing" it. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/rough-sleeping-homeless-law-vagrancy-act-b3004459.html (''The Independent'')]
